nodes.title: MDA / IMS-MDA / MIDAS
nodes.scope: Illumina grouped explanatory schematic of genomic-DNA multiple displacement amplification and explicitly supported MDA, IMS-MDA and MIDAS contexts. The complete drawn route is Genome → Hybridize primers → two successive illustrations of Phi29 Synthesis, with displacement and secondary priming → S1 nuclease → Amplified DNA. There are no drawn alternative workflow branches; raised DNA branches are molecular intermediates, not separate cell populations. The product shown is amplified genomic DNA, not an adapter-bearing sequencing library. Preserve the diagram’s 3′blocked primer wording as an observation and resolve it from the MDA paper as exonuclease protection with an extendable primer. op_s1 remains a family-level depicted operation with unresolved MDA/IMS-MDA applicability; the supported MIDAS recovery and Polymerase I route is explicitly distinguished as paper-only context. IMS capture and microwell confinement are method distinctions established by primary content, not visual features added to the diagram. The catalogue card contains no method body, so it supplies no additional reaction sequence. No historical development or interchangeability between the named implementations is asserted.

In the inspected Chlamydia trachomatis study, antibodies associated with magnetic beads capture intact target bacteria (the reported primary antibody targets LPS); lysis and genomic-DNA denaturation then supply the MDA substrate. Amplification is performed on the retained beads without elution. These upstream context steps distinguish the variant but are not drawn as separate panels. MDA is the shared molecular copying core. Enrichment does not produce a pure target sample, and downstream sequencing can retain contaminant DNA and uneven genome coverage. The protocol PMID 24202554 supplies only abstract-level corroboration of IMS → MDA → sequencing. No supplied primary content establishes the S1 arrow as required for IMS-MDA; its applicability remains unresolved.

Limited amplification occurs in individual nanoliter microwells, and selected amplicons are recovered separately; this physical association underlies a cell-specific genomic readout. Sparse loading and amplicon selection support single-cell attribution without making every microwell intrinsically single-cell or every genomic locus equally represented.
